findings.message: Over 2857 ms the CPU was busy 26% and 27 outbound network calls took 568 ms combined.
Of the 574 ms render: load functions 33.2 ms + 389 ms waiting · other 52.5 ms + 10.4 ms waiting · component render 37.2 ms · ogygia transform 21.3 ms · remote functions 0.23 ms + 18.6 ms waiting.

6 calls ran one after another for 298 ms: GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/session, GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/pricing, GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/inventory, timer · rows (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:13), queue.drain, timer · value (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:59). Started together they would cost 99.9 ms — about 199 ms saved.
findings.fix: Start them together (Promise.all) when they are independent; a call that needs an earlier result stays sequential.

findings.message: 16 calls to 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/product/:id — one per item, 131 ms together.
findings.fix: Batch them: one request with the ids (or a bulk endpoint), or fetch the list with its children included.

findings.message: Biggest CPU consumer: node core (156 ms, 21.3% of busy time).
One render of Root costs 156 ms (21.3% of busy).
findings.fix: Compute the expensive part once (in load, or a per-request cache) and pass the result as a prop, or render it in a deferred hole.

findings.message: stock.lookup ran 16 times in one render (load (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:77)), 128 ms together, 7.87 ms each.
findings.fix: Once per item is the N+1 shape: batch it (one call for all the ids), or fetch the parent with its children included.

findings.message: ogygia added 14.4 ms to the render: 51 islands, seed 254 KB, props 125 KB, remote seed 164 B.
The page seed is 254 KB: an island reads $page, so that much of page.data ships to the browser and is serialized on every render.
findings.fix: Read only the keys the island needs (page.data.x, not page.data) so seed shaping trims it, or pass the values as props.

findings.message: PriceTicker, ProductCard read page.data whole, so every key ships in the seed (254 KB, the biggest is catalog at 225 KB).
findings.fix: Read the keys by name (page.data.catalog, not a spread or a loop over page.data) so seed shaping can drop the rest, or pass the values in as props.

findings.message: The seed (254 KB) left the JSON lane because of catalog.facets (Map) — devalue writes and revives it several times slower than JSON.parse.
findings.fix: Send that value as a plain string or number (a Date as toISOString(), a Map as an object), or keep it out of page.data.

findings.message: MegaHeader's props (111 KB) use devalue because of config.updated (Date).
findings.fix: JSON props parse on the fast lane in the browser: pass the value as a string or number, or derive it inside the island.

findings.message: ProductCard has 48 copies on the page, each waking on visible with its own 80 B of props.
findings.fix: One island around the list hydrates once; or wake: 'interaction' so a copy pays only when touched.

findings.message: Hole 01d4f0f09349: 2 of 3 requests served from the render cache (maxAge 300s).
1 hole renders fresh on every visit (97f70770dcf8 50.9 ms).
findings.fix: Content that is the same for every visitor for a while can take a maxAge: the endpoint then serves the memo.

findings.message: In the browser, 3 islands reported hydration: 91.7 ms in all (p50), the slowest ProductCard at 57.9 ms.
findings.fix: The hydrate step itself is slow: fewer elements per island, or split the island so the interactive part is small.

findings.message: _page renders 48 ProductCard rows per render, 23.4 ms together (0.49 ms each).
findings.fix: The list is the cost, not the row: page it, window it, or defer the part below the fold into a hole.

findings.message: 201 ms of busy time is the profiler itself — a one-time cost when recording starts. Your app did not pay this outside the recording.
